causes.where: imas_codex/standard_names/review/cascade.py -- _docs_judgment raises ValueError('no usable judgment for documentation review'), which adjudicate_review catches and records as the fallback's reason
causes.mechanism: The documentation judging batch returned no result for the item, so _docs_judgment raised. The item fell back to the incumbent, and because that fallback produced a result an unjudged shadow row was written carrying the exception's text -- which is why only these items carry a reason at all.
causes.root_cause: decide_batch reports a failed call as None rather than raising. The one line it writes for that is 'decision batch item 0 failed: ' with an empty fault string, and the call layer's retry policy is a substring match over that message -- an empty message matches no pattern, so the fault is classified non-retryable and the call raises on its first attempt. The absence of any 'decisions error (attempt' line in the run log is what proves the retry never fired.

causes.where: docs/evidence/fragments/sn-review-through-jev/srtj-cohort-run.py -- the runner falls back to the literal string 'no route row' when an unjudged item carries no failure reason
causes.mechanism: The item carries route unjudged and an empty failure reason. The composition writes a shadow row carrying a reason only when the incumbent fallback returned a result; when the fallback also returned nothing, no row is written at all and the runner reports the empty reason as 'no route row'.
causes.root_cause: The fallback is the paid panel quorum, whose seats this run's budget refused: the log reads 'rd_quorum docs cycle 0 unfunded for <id> (model=...): the run budget could not reserve $0.05xx of pre-launch exposure -- the reviewer was never called', followed by 'rd_quorum docs incomplete: 0/3 reviews succeeded for <id> -- deferring, NOT accepting on a single review (budget refused 1 seat(s))'. The dry run's own stop reason is time_limit_reached with cost_spent 1.84 against a cost_limit of 1.90, so the batch was cut short before these items were reached: almost all carry calls == 0, i.e. no Jev call was ever made for them.

classes.class: mechanical hold: score lands on the cutoff
classes.owner: the incumbent's recorded score, not a substantive judgment
classes.mechanism: The incumbent's stored score sits at or a thousandth below the min_score the pair is scored against (0.85), so the pair is counted as disagreement on the score's own arithmetic edge rather than on a difference in judgment. The value is the incumbent row's aggregate over its own dimension scores, not Jev's: across these items only a minority of scores coincide between the two arms.

classes.class: not readable from the record: incumbent reason line absent
classes.owner: the collector's record, not the incumbent's judgment
classes.mechanism: The incumbent arm's piece files persist summary fields only (axis, calls, chat_reviewer_called, decision, docs_stage_at_draw, failure_reason, id, name_stage_at_draw, route, score, spend_usd, wall_time_s). No comment, hold note or cap note survives in any artifact, so whether these items were refined for a defect in the text or for a mechanical reason cannot be settled from what is on the branch.
classes.missing_evidence: The review rows the incumbent wrote went into each piece's own scratch graph, which the pieces record as removed, and the arm's run logs carry neither item ids nor comment text. The live graph's stored documentation reviews predate the cohort dump and disagree with the score the pieces persist, so they are not a substitute for the missing rows. Reporting these as substantive would be a guess.
